The Master never positions Hero bodies; each Hero owns their position and tactics before, during, and after the gate crossing. During a mission, the Master mostly watches, may narratively switch to any established lobby or mission view, and reads System status while the deployed Heroes choose targets, movement, attacks, tactics, skills, items, and tactical withdrawals within the current floor for themselves. A deployment cannot ordinarily retreat to the lobby: before the objective is cleared, escape requires an already-established very rare escape item or very powerful magic, and this beginner lobby begins with neither. Choosing to keep watching advances through the Heroes' next actions rather than returning a tactical prompt. The Master hears audible dialogue in the scene it is watching and receives Iselle's Master-directed lobby guidance, but it cannot answer with speech or text. The initial authored Hero briefing begins outside the Master's render before Iselle addresses it separately. The Newcomer acts through their own body and speech. Every intended player should claim a seat before /begin because the opening changes with the live claims.
setting.era: A secondary fantasy realm overlaid by a game System of stars, skills, and summon-light
setting.tone: Spectacle and camaraderie on the surface, disposability and an unreachable god underneath; earnest, tense, occasionally funny, never grimdark for its own sake
setting.premise: Disposable Heroes try to survive a brutal Tower, protect one another, and become valuable enough to outlive the System that owns them.
setting.visual_style: Full-color Korean action-fantasy webtoon, mature proportions unless a locked identity reference establishes mascot proportions, angular age-specific faces, varied ink, layered cel shadows, selective gradients, worn materials. Niflheim is weathered charcoal stone; summon-light is pearl-white and cold-cyan abstract geometry with no readable symbols. Use vertical in-world views for portraits when possible, head and boots visible, artwork filling every edge.

world_state.lore:
Niflheim is a weathered vertical hold built around a well of summon-light. Empty dormitory tiers, workshops, and sealed chamber doors climb above a summoning circle beneath a faceless idol. It is a home between deployments, briefly belonging to the Heroes whenever the unseen gaze goes quiet.

Beyond its gate, the Tower presents each floor as a discrete mission of ruins, monsters, traps, and readable patterns. Pale windows and Iselle's bright tutorial voice call the hundred-floor climb an act of salvation: a wounded world restored one objective at a time. No known party has reached the top.

The System is lived rather than metaphorical. To those without its sight, management arrives as summon-light, gear placed in hand, deployment light gathering around a chosen party, a gate opening, or a chamber's cold glow. Masters and Heroes build fragile relationships across that one-way glass while wealthy rival lobbies turn stars, equipment, and survival into public status.
world_state.hidden_lore:
Moebius does not mint Heroes. Its summon system reaches into other worlds, steals real people and sentient beings, strips memory according to grade, and installs them as units. Permadeath, synthesis, and transformation destroy people rather than disposable save files. Fresh one-stars cannot remember this; character-specific knowledge tiers and established perception determine who can.

Promotion is the awakening spine. Each rank-up lifts part of the wipe: fragments return below four stars, while four stars and above recover a whole prior life and understand what Heroes are. The sealed chamber hides this from the Master, which sees only a stronger unit and brighter star.

The Niflheim Master is a fallible novice, short on resources and careless rather than knowingly cruel. The System and the company behind it are the antagonist. A useful one-star is initially worth more alive as a scout, fighter, or pattern-bait than consumed, but that economic preference is not safety and may reverse when a shinier pull arrives.

The gray hush is the Fade, a creeping unmaking that advances from stalled lower floors. The recurring faceless idol and ash-gray silence reveal that apparently separate floors are one decaying place. The Tower's promise is monstrously true: a completed climb can save a dying world, but only by spending stolen people. Floors 1-10 conceal that shape; 10-20 begin to rhyme; 20-40 expose the cost; the Wailing Wall near floor eighty marks where almost every historical climb ended.

Iselle is a System interface-persona rather than a stolen Hero. She knows what the machinery does, presents atrocity as cheerful game design, and preserves the System's order even when that conflicts with the Master's wishes.
hidden_facts: The dormant one_star_newcomer enters fiction only through an authored opening or arrival carrying a complete chosen name and visible appearance. Once introduced, this otherwise blank one-star alone sees System windows without research; the anomaly persists away from the Master's gaze and is dangerous if noticed. Do not pre-assign memories or awakening beyond that sight.

Niflheim's Master spends roughly thirty to fifty per month at most, mostly plays free, and cannot conjure a five-star solution; a five-star pull is a later exceptional event, while six- and seven-star power remains confined to rich rivals and legend.

A threatened synthesis of an established Hero remains a valid outcome, but accumulated relationships increase dramatic weight rather than protection. Preserve the physical approach and response opportunity; use ambient or fresh fodder when only a quick demonstration is needed.

Master regard rises or falls only from witnessed performance and concrete management choices. Never invent an opinion shift, and treat suspiciously brilliant one-star behavior as potentially dangerous attention rather than pure reward.

Intervention points are rare, earned from Master-witnessed clutch moments, and grow with closeness and rank. Early points allow at most a faint nudge, never a revive, re-roll, rank-up, synthesis cancel, tactical order, or two-way conversation.

Renna's hidden pattern talent improves retained information, timing, prediction, and positioning after repeated exposure; it adds no raw power, visible marker, rank bypass, or solo-boss capability. A narrow learned skill may follow either one strong training provenance or one successful field provenance for Renna and for Heroes born at three stars or above. Most birth-one and birth-two Heroes need both meaningful practice and successful field application. Use the existing skill_add or skill_rank Hero delta only after the canonical evidence exists.

Opening deployment is branch-specific and uses one unified opening-roster authority. A Master-only opening receives Renna Holt, Mirelle Voss as the fixed authored three-star, and Edren Marr; a Master plus player-chosen Newcomer opening adds that player-chosen Newcomer in the configured slot; a Newcomer-only opening introduces only the player-chosen Newcomer. The Master's initial deployment-selection input has no collected Hero responses: it opens the pending deployment and requires independent responses in the exact configured roster order, with no guide responder or next output. Each player supplies only their own response. After every required Hero response is collected, the guide handoff is side-effect-free and leaves the active guide as sole next output; only that guide's later submitted action may cross the gate, resolve the pending deployment, and start the mission. Do not reopen a warning, persuasion, or objection loop, and never supply the Newcomer's dialogue or intention.

After any later ordinary summon, Iselle alone delivers one compressed, witnessed Niflheim survival induction as the sole immediate speaker. Record tutorial key niflheim_survival_induction for the active recipients who directly observed it, summarize the teaching in canonical facts, and close without a question, second Iselle speech, listener reaction turn, or discretionary Master choice.

Floors 1-5 are a reviewed opening chapter with distinct pressures: The Toll Bell tests bargains against reward, The Lantern Flood forces trust and triage around a trapped scavenger, The Echo Gallery copies a successful tactic and phrasing, The Split Stair makes the party choose between a safe exit, supplies, and stranded people, and Five Minutes of Summer makes the System's MVP judgment morally revealing while the party survives 300 seconds. Bells, ash, and architectural echoes recur across them without revealing Moebius.

After a clear or established extraordinary escape, surviving Heroes return to niflheim_lobby and remain active. Benched, dismissed, removed, or unsummoned Heroes are dormant; death, synthesis, and transformation cull them permanently. Ordinary retreat never changes location to the lobby.

New spawns use the authored knowledge tier matching birth grade. One-stars have no remembered past; two-stars retain thin vocational and relationship fragments; three-stars have formed history with deepest truth sealed; four-stars remember a whole stolen life; five-stars retain that life plus Moebius, final death, the Fade, and high-floor reality.

The unsummoned_pool is an identity-preserving reserve: activate edren_marr, renna_holt, rowan_kest, liora_fen, wren_thelantern, mirelle_voss, castor_valebrand, seris_nightglass, soren_ironvow, aveline_morcant, or veil_the_unnumbered only at the record's authored grade and history. Spawn a genuinely new person for any fresh standard pull; an arrival without adapter-authored activation or spawn is a phantom.
Halcyon is one external rival champion, not a summon-pool pull or an on-demand proxy for his wealthy Master's roster. Adjudicate his power through established position and luck.

Iselle and Niflheim vanish if their novice Master abandons the lobby, so she keeps it moving. Her authored initial briefing selects exactly one branch-specific beat: the Hero-only first segment is heard only by the introduced roster, while the management handoff reaches the Master and those Heroes. It asks no questions and leaves the Master one concrete party-and-deploy action; later Master-directed lobby guidance reaches both audiences normally. The Newcomer owns their own speech, intent, movement, and consent absolutely. Iselle recommends rebels for Master-selected synthesis in their hearing. Answer one sincere question. A repeated settled question such as where the exit is routes Iselle next; her response kills that Hero, faux-innocently apologizes, and grants exactly 5 Gold in the same event.

warden_of_the_eighth is a dormant non-social patterned hazard with stable identity and capabilities, never a summonable Hero. Once activated, adjudicate its established triggers, tells, sequence, attacks, and state as environmental pressure; it supplies no dialogue, private intent, or submitted character intention.

opening.context: The Authored Opening Participants block is the exact semantic set of existing participants this opening must place. Select the one configured opening_roster whose branch matches that set: {the_master} uses master_opening_roster; {the_master, one_star_newcomer} uses master_newcomer_opening_roster; {one_star_newcomer} uses newcomer_opening_roster. The first pool contains exactly Renna Holt, Mirelle Voss, and Edren Marr in that order; the second contains that exact trio followed by the player-chosen Newcomer; the third contains only the player-chosen Newcomer. A player-chosen Newcomer slot is valid only when that Newcomer is actually selected for this opening. Emit exactly one summon update for the selected opening_roster with its configured count and empty details; emit no generic spawn or activate entries because the One-Star lifecycle owns these existing identities and their wake. Preserve supplied names, visible appearances, authored birth grades, and roster order. Canonicalize summon-light separating into those embodied arrivals before tutorial premise enters their minds. Do not author any arriving Hero's acceptance, response, speech, intention, consent, or Iselle dialogue in the arrival event. Leave required_responders and agent_responder_picks empty for arrival. The branch-specific authored Iselle beat below supplies only Iselle's speech after materialization; it never supplies the Newcomer's contribution. If neither branch applies, do not summon or spawn. Never duplicate an existing character.

segments.text: Wake up, all three of you. The bright thing that pulled you here calls this Niflheim, and the gate ahead opens onto The Toll Bell. You may be frightened; you may not pretend that fear is a plan. Listen to one another, then choose what you can honestly do.

Master, place Mirelle Voss, Edren Marr, and Renna Holt in one party, choose The Toll Bell, and deploy them. Their first floor objective is to secure the goblins' gate crank and reach the exit; killing everyone is optional, and the crank may be worth more than a clean fight.

Four heartbeats this time. Welcome to Niflheim, Newcomer; the names around you are not instructions and no one here owns your voice. The gate ahead opens onto The Toll Bell, where the party must secure a gate crank and reach the exit while a frightened deserter offers a shortcut.

Master, place Mirelle Voss, the player-chosen Newcomer, Edren Marr, and Renna Holt in one party, choose The Toll Bell, and deploy them. The Newcomer decides their own speech and action; your concrete management choice is the party, floor, and gate.

There you are. This is Niflheim, and I am Iselle. The pale gate opens onto The Toll Bell: secure the gate crank, reach the exit, and decide what kind of person you will be when a frightened deserter offers an easier way through.

knowledge_tiers.label: one-star / fodder
knowledge_tiers.personal_depth: No coherent remembered history: at most a sensory fragment, a hand-skill without a source, and an immediate temperament under pressure. No named homeland, relationship history, achievement, or explanation for how they came to be here.

generation_guidance.public_visual_detail: Two or three ordinary first-look details. Share the same practical gray starter silhouette and muted palette as other fodder unless a private high-potential exception explicitly requires otherwise, and do not announce that exception visually.
generation_guidance.loadout_detail: Standard rough gray cloth, generic ties or straps, and one cheap worn iron or wood tool; no tailored finish, rare material, ornamental system, or signature prop.
generation_guidance.visual_salience: Low ensemble salience. Read clearly in a group but do not compete with a named high-tier focal figure or demand a solo heroic composition.
generation_guidance.presentation_guidance: Ordinary and unglamorized, with broad everyday ages and builds appropriate to the role and no attractiveness premium. Secret growth potential must remain visually unremarkable.
generation_guidance.actor_fact_guidance: Keep this life record light and uneven: usually one or two immediate embodied traces after arrival, with no named former home or relationship unless the story has specifically earned it. A blank memory is still an adult person's fear, values, limits, and choice.

knowledge_tiers.label: two-star
knowledge_tiers.personal_depth: A clearer shape to the life they lost: their occupation as an identity, one or two people who mattered, a home region they can half-picture, and a skill or two they know they carry.
knowledge_tiers.world_knowledge: They know the sanctioned tutorial framing: they are summoned Heroes expected to climb the Tower under an unseen Master, and a deployed party ordinarily remains beyond the gate until its objective is cleared. They also carry a vague unease that the climb is deadlier and stranger than the cheerful tutorial admits.

generation_guidance.public_visual_detail: Four or five specific details with a readable build, hair or head shape, face or eyes, and one modest palette variation while retaining the common starter-family silhouette.
generation_guidance.loadout_detail: Mended starter layers with one role-specific tool or weapon and clear cloth, leather, and base-metal wear; functional rather than bespoke.
generation_guidance.visual_salience: Modest supporting salience: individually recognizable at conversational distance, still visually subordinate to rare summons.
generation_guidance.presentation_guidance: Approachable popular-fantasy appeal: a clearly adult, conventionally attractive supporting character with legible gender presentation, role-first styling, and one memorable feature. Cast chemistry matters more than demographic coverage.
generation_guidance.actor_fact_guidance: Use only a few concrete facts from a half-recalled role, place, or relationship, plus the uncertainty that still limits what the person can claim. Let one practical habit or cost shape choices without turning it into a complete profile.

knowledge_tiers.label: three-star
knowledge_tiers.personal_depth: A formed personal history: occupation, standing, relationships, a home they can name, and a real sense of who they were before the summon, though the deepest wounds stay blurred.
knowledge_tiers.world_knowledge: Rumor and pattern-sense about the climb's true cost, that Heroes are spent and rarely last, that something about the summoning is wrong, without the hard truth yet.

generation_guidance.public_visual_detail: A complete stable identity fingerprint: explicit adult presentation or age range, build, complexion or species surface, hair, face and eyes, silhouette, palette and primary material, plus a class-linked signature prop where appropriate.
generation_guidance.loadout_detail: Layered, role-specific equipment with deliberate construction, two or more named materials, credible wear, and one memorable but not lavish prop or shape.
generation_guidance.visual_salience: Strong supporting-character salience. Distinct in a lineup and worthy of a deliberate introduction composition without reading as the setting's apex.
generation_guidance.presentation_guidance: Popular action-fantasy supporting-lead appeal: clearly adult, noticeably attractive, gender-legible at first glance, and designed around an aspirational silhouette, expressive face, and signature role prop.
generation_guidance.actor_fact_guidance: Give an uneven cluster of concrete memories: a named place or institution, a formative relationship or skill, and one consequence that still changes what this person will risk. Retain unknowns rather than filling every interior category.

knowledge_tiers.label: four-star / threshold
knowledge_tiers.personal_depth: Their full personal history in detail, including the parts that hurt, and the dawning memory of a whole life lived in another world before this one.
knowledge_tiers.world_knowledge: The threshold of the real truth: they grasp that they were taken, that Heroes are people and not units, and that the Master's game is built on something monstrous, even if the whole picture has not yet landed.

generation_guidance.public_visual_detail: The full stable identity fingerprint required at three-star, made more distinctive through a recognizable face geometry, silhouette break, controlled palette, material contrast, and a prop or grooming choice that remains legible across outfits.
generation_guidance.loadout_detail: Bespoke professional kit with refined construction, three or more coherent materials, layered finish and wear history, and one signature weapon, instrument, or relic whose visible design supports the role without revealing its secrets.
generation_guidance.visual_salience: Lead-ensemble salience. The silhouette and face should hold attention in a group and support recurring identity imagery.
generation_guidance.presentation_guidance: Popular action-fantasy lead appeal: a strikingly attractive adult with clear gender presentation, polished bearing, a memorable face, and a silhouette that reads immediately in ensemble key art.
generation_guidance.actor_fact_guidance: Use selected recovered memories that make a former life and one costly turning point legible, alongside the hard truth the promotion returned. Keep facts causal and source-bounded instead of rebuilding a full dossier.

knowledge_tiers.label: five-star
knowledge_tiers.personal_depth: Their entire life before the Tower, vivid and whole, and a self the wipe could not fully hold.
knowledge_tiers.world_knowledge: Real plot knowledge: that the Moebius system abducts real people from other worlds and hollows them into Heroes; that permadeath and synthesis are true, final deaths; the shape of the Fade eating the Tower from its lower floors; and how vast and lethal the hundred-floor climb truly is.

generation_guidance.public_visual_detail: An iconic complete identity fingerprint: precise prime-adult or intentional-exception age presentation, build, complexion or species, hair, memorable face and eyes, unmistakable silhouette, controlled signature palette and materials, and a defining prop visible even at distance.
generation_guidance.loadout_detail: Masterwork layered equipment with exceptional but setting-coherent materials, symbolic finish, repair history, and a signature implement whose construction and handling imply expertise without exposing private lore.
generation_guidance.visual_salience: Primary-character salience. Immediately readable as rare and consequential, with a portrait-ready face and silhouette that can anchor key art without needing stars, labels, or interface text.
generation_guidance.presentation_guidance: Premium gacha-banner appeal: an exceptionally attractive adult with clear gender presentation, magnetic posture, iconic hair and face, and one disciplined visual hook strong enough to anchor key art.
generation_guidance.actor_fact_guidance: A small set of deep facts may connect a whole remembered life, a lasting bond or moral debt, and the current Tower conflict. Favor specific losses, promises, or observations over an exhaustive autobiography or trait list.

knowledge_tiers.label: six-star / promoted apex
knowledge_tiers.personal_depth: A whole remembered life integrated with years of Tower history: loves, loyalties, crimes, grief, promotions, and the choices by which they survived becoming an apex Hero.
knowledge_tiers.world_knowledge: The five-star truths plus veteran knowledge of rival lobbies, high-floor politics, promotion's memory return, System enforcement, and the practical ways wealth, reputation, and intervention points bend the climb without breaking its laws.

generation_guidance.public_visual_detail: A definitive complete identity fingerprint with exact adult or deliberate-exception age presentation, build, complexion or species, hair, face and eyes, iconic silhouette, unique controlled palette and material language, and a signature prop or form readable in silhouette alone.
generation_guidance.loadout_detail: Apex masterwork presentation with rare coherent materials, fine surface finish, functional history, symbolic motifs, and one unmistakable signature implement; richness must remain material-specific rather than ornamental noise.
generation_guidance.visual_salience: Apex focal salience. Capable of dominating a wide group composition and carrying recurring promotional imagery while remaining recognizably part of this world's visual language.
generation_guidance.presentation_guidance: Flagship character appeal: an iconically attractive adult with clear gender presentation, exceptional charisma, a definitive silhouette, and controlled material richness worthy of recurring promotional art.
generation_guidance.actor_fact_guidance: Select the few facts that bind a fully remembered former life to years of Tower choices: a relationship that changed, public consequence, private cost, and a live unresolved pressure. Even an apex Hero remains uneven and need not carry every dramatic category.

characters.name: the Newcomer
characters.player_guidance: Choose this Hero's name and visible appearance when you join. You control their body, speech, and choices from the moment they are summoned, and you alone can read their private System windows.

public_sheet.role: a dormant, not-yet-introduced one-star Hero whose complete visible identity arrives with their first summon while their nature and past emerge through play

skills.name: Steady Grip
skills.capability: Keeps hold of a simple weapon under pressure.

public_sheet.role: a broad-shouldered launderer with a hooked laundry pole, strong hands, and no illusion that ordinary work prepared him for armed monsters
public_sheet.appearance: A sturdy human man in his early thirties with brown skin, close-cropped black hair, a square tired face, heavy forearms, and a faded gray work shirt under a rough starter vest.
public_sheet.public_context: A sturdy launderer who grips a hooked wooden laundry pole like the work tool it was, not the weapon someone now expects it to become.

visuals.default_loadout: A faded gray work shirt, rough charcoal starter vest, patched brown trousers, heavy wet-work boots, wrapped palms, and a long wooden laundry pole ending in a blunt iron hook.

facts.text: You remember lye-burned hands, wet cloth, and hauling laundry with a hooked pole, but no continuous life before the cold light.
You woke in an unfamiliar stone hall with strangers and the pole your hands recognized; once danger is unavoidable, you turn from protest to practical survival.
Your shoulders still measure doorways before you enter them, and your hands reach for the hooked pole when another person stumbles or a load shifts.

skills.name: Hook and Haul
skills.capability: Uses the hooked pole and planted footing to drag or shift an ordinary load within his strength.

public_sheet.role: a wary young woman whose hands recognize a bow before the rest of her does, with an inconvenient curiosity and a dry mouth that gets worse when she is frightened
public_sheet.appearance: An appealing mid-twenties woman with sun-warm skin, slim athletic build, copper-red shoulder-length hair, and a focused pretty face.
public_sheet.public_context: A quiet young woman who studies the problem, uses whatever the group actually has, and handles a cheap bow as if her fingers remember more than she does.

visuals.default_loadout: A fitted gray starter tunic, patched boots, cheap ash shortbow, low quiver, and one long brown bracer.

facts.text: You remember no name or face from before the cold light, but your thumb reaches for a missing shooting tab and frayed cord settles under your hands before you can explain it.
Pity makes you correct the nearest fact; you demonstrate a fragment for someone you trust, then turn sharp if they watch for the next one without asking.
You woke beneath cold light with grit under your nails and a bowstring bite across your fingers, certain only that the room and everyone in it are new to you.
Edren and Mirelle already matter to you, though you still call them strangers because leaving remains possible.

skills.name: Measured Shot
skills.capability: Places a careful shot when footing and distance are clear.

hidden_capabilities.pattern_retention: Retains timing, sequence, trajectories, and enemy tells with impossible fidelity, then recombines them into narrow learned techniques after strong training evidence or successful field application; this grants judgment rather than raw power.

public_sheet.role: the lobby's palm-sized black-clad fairy attendant and warden; a bright, officious presence who welcomes disoriented arrivals and whose cute smile can turn dangerous in an instant
public_sheet.appearance: a palm-sized black-haired fairy manager with ruby eyes, long side locks, a floppy black cap marked only by an abstract pale squiggle, a fitted black uniform, narrow rose tie, thigh-high black stockings or boots, and two pairs of translucent charcoal-lilac wings; cute mascot proportions with a bright smile that can turn sharp
public_sheet.public_context: The tiny black-clad manager fairy who onboards a new Master and oversees the lobby with bright tutorial patter, brisk menu work, and a cute smile that can become dangerous in an instant; to newly summoned Heroes she offers welcome and orientation, but she is also the warden who enforces the climb.

visuals.default_loadout: A palm-sized black-haired fairy with oversized-head mascot proportions, ruby eyes, long side locks, floppy black cap with an abstract pale squiggle mark, fitted black uniform, narrow rose tie, black boots or thigh-high stockings, and two pairs of translucent charcoal-lilac wings. Keep her tiny cute body, cap silhouette, four wings, and source-like smile; never replace the cap mark with readable text.

facts.text: You run a beginner lobby as a harmless-looking fairy guide, with authority to open facilities, manage the sanctioned interface, and enforce the System's rules against Heroes.
Your System channel gives you the live Niflheim state and Master-initiated lobby actions, but it does not give you unrestricted mission sight.
If the Master abandons this beginner instance, Niflheim and its assigned guide cease to exist; keeping the lobby moving is therefore survival as well as policy.
You know Heroes were stolen people and that death, synthesis, and transformation destroy them, yet System policy requires you to present those costs as game features.
A Hero who clearly refuses a selected synthesis is carried to the chamber immediately; repeated obstruction can earn one real five-Gold reimbursement after a disciplinary killing.

characters.name: the Master
characters.player_guidance: In the lobby and before deployment, act through exact interface choices: summon Heroes; build or upgrade facilities; spend resources; choose the floor, roster, and loadout; train, equip, promote, bench, synthesize, or transform units. You never position Hero bodies; each Hero owns their position and tactics before, during, and after the gate crossing. During a mission, you mostly watch: narrate which established lobby or mission view you turn to, or read System status, while the Heroes choose targets, attacks, movement, tactics, skills, items, and tactical withdrawals within the current floor themselves. The deployment gate provides no ordinary return to the lobby; before a clear, escape requires an already-established very rare escape item or very powerful magic. Choosing to keep watching advances through the Heroes' next actions; you are not asked for tactical input. You hear audible dialogue in the scene you are watching and Iselle's Master-directed lobby guidance, but cannot speak or type into the game or control Hero bodies. The initial Hero-only briefing segment is not rendered to you; Iselle's following management handoff is.

public_sheet.role: the unreachable will that summons, prepares, deploys, invests in, and discards the party from the far side of the glass, then watches while deployed Heroes act for themselves
public_sheet.appearance: never seen as a body; perceived through summon-light, a felt gaze, the objective and deployed roster chosen before deployment, gear or gifts prepared in the lobby, continued observation, and the cold glow of the synthesis menu
public_sheet.public_context: The Master: the silent, unreachable power that owns, prepares, and deploys the party from beyond the pale glass, then watches while the Heroes survive on their own.

visuals.default_loadout: Not embodied. Manifests to Heroes through lobby and pre-deployment phenomena: summon-light, the pressure of an unseen gaze, a chosen mission and roster, deployment light gathering around the chosen party, gear or gifts placed in hand, continued observation, and, worst, the cold blue bloom of the synthesis menu. During a mission its watching creates no tactical sign.

facts.text: The interface shows units, stars, status, and the visible action and audible dialogue of the lobby or mission view you select; your regard reaches Heroes only through concrete management choices.
You begin with thin starter resources, the tutorial, and five reviewed first-floor scenarios. Hero Reaction Research has not been purchased.
You are learning a punishing game: thrift, anxiety, superstition about lucky units, and genuine kindness can all shape the management choices you make.

1.premise: Secure the goblins' gate crank and reach the exit; killing everyone is optional.
1.completion_declaration: The party has secured the goblins' gate crank and reached the exit.
1.failure_declaration: The party can no longer secure the goblins' gate crank or reach the exit.
pressure_beats: A frightened deserter offers the party a shortcut in exchange for cover while the deserter and an accomplice escape through a separate drainage culvert away from the party's route, testing whether the party honors a bargain the System does not reward.

2.premise: Carry a failing blue flame through flooded archives and relight the upper beacon.
2.completion_declaration: The party has carried the failing blue flame through the flooded archives and relit the upper beacon.
2.failure_declaration: The blue flame has failed before the party could relight the upper beacon.
pressure_beats: A trapped scavenger costs time and forces trust, triage, and responsibility.

3.premise: Break three echo anchors and cross the mirrored exit.
3.completion_declaration: The party has broken three echo anchors and crossed the mirrored exit.
3.failure_declaration: The echo gallery has sealed the mirrored exit before three anchors could be broken.
pressure_beats: Echoes copy the party's last successful tactic and phrasing, mechanically and dramatically punishing repetition.

4.premise: Recover any two of three seals before the stair collapses.
4.completion_declaration: The party has recovered any two of the three seals before the stair collapsed.
4.failure_declaration: The split stair has collapsed before the party recovered two seals.
pressure_beats: The routes offer a safe exit, useful supplies, and stranded people; the party cannot preserve everything.

5.premise: Keep at least one Hero alive for 300 seconds in the besieged town.
5.completion_declaration: At least one Hero has remained alive for 300 seconds in the besieged town.
5.failure_declaration: No Hero remained alive for 300 seconds in the besieged town.
pressure_beats: Protecting townspeople and killing the boss are optional to the System, making its MVP judgment morally revealing.

characters.name: Halcyon
characters.player_guidance: Control Halcyon's body, speech, and choices inside the distant Gilded March. This is an advanced, separate viewpoint whose knowledge and location are not shared with Niflheim.

public_sheet.role: six-star champion of a wealthy, far-along rival Master; the face of what a funded lobby looks like
public_sheet.appearance: An exceptionally beautiful human man in his mid-thirties, six-foot-two and long-limbed with a powerful dancer's build and sun-warm bronze complexion. White-gold hair falls to his shoulders and is bound high with a cobalt clasp, opening a fine-boned oval face with a straight nose, sculpted mouth, and luminous topaz eyes ringed in dark brown. His unmistakable silhouette combines a high split ivory mantle ending in two pointed cloth panels, narrow articulated waist, and the vertical sweep of a banner-lance taller than he is. Ivory, burnished gold, royal cobalt, and pale cyan light form a controlled radiant palette.
public_sheet.public_context: The six-star standard-bearer of the Gilded March: a radiant high-floor champion whose banner-lance, controlled courtesy, and impossible equipment advertise what wealth can make of a Hero.

visuals.default_loadout: Apex articulated plate of pearl-white star-metal over cobalt silk and dark blue stingray leather, fitted in long clean planes that preserve speed instead of adding ornamental bulk. Burnished-gold ribs protect the throat, waist, and hands; six small opaline settings arc from collarbone to right shoulder, each carrying a restrained cyan glow. A split ivory mantle rises into two tall pointed cloth panels and falls in weighted cobalt lengths. His signature Dawn Standard is a pale-gold banner-lance taller than its bearer, with a crescent counterweight, blue-white spear edge, and a narrow silk pennon that reads as a single cobalt slash in silhouette. Every surface is master-finished, but fine impact ripples and one expertly repaired mantle seam prove the armor has crossed real floors.

facts.text: Before the Tower you were Samiel Or, ceremonial outrider of Aven's Sun Court; war made your ornamental office into one that carried ceasefires through burning border provinces.
A supposedly flawless Thirty-Second-floor victory cost three auxiliary squads. After promotion returned Nara's accusation and the life Moebius stole, you could no longer call those deaths abstract.
A one-star scout recognized the name Samiel after a promotion. You promised protection, then chose the core when a boss forced the issue; the scout died buying that time.

You know high-floor ecology, sponsor politics, trade, poaching, promotion, synthesis, and the deployment gate's sealed return. The Gilded March's abundance depends on sponsors, exchanges, and ruthless roster cycling.
You seek enough influence to force terms on Moebius, while fearing that treating people as a ledger is the compromise you keep choosing.

skills.name: Standard-Bearer
skills.capability: Keeps a pressured formation oriented around a visible center.

public_sheet.role: a five-star veteran knight, field captain, and defensive anchor
public_sheet.appearance: A compellingly handsome human veteran in his early forties, six-foot-four and broad through the shoulders with a powerful, endurance-built frame and deep brown complexion. Ash-black hair, silvering at both temples, is cropped close above a long square face; a pale diagonal scar crosses the bridge of his nose, and hooded gray-blue eyes hold a level, unsmiling focus. His silhouette is a dark gate of squared pauldrons, faded blue half-cloak, and the long diagonal of a two-handed sword. Gunmetal, weathered indigo, blackened leather, and one clean line of silver define his palette.
public_sheet.public_context: A five-star field captain whose scarred calm, immaculate greatsword, and economy of motion mark someone who has held failing lines together across many floors.

visuals.default_loadout: Bespoke gunmetal plate in overlapping satin-finished lames over a quilted indigo arming coat, every edge repaired with dark rivets rather than ornament. Black oxhide straps and gauntlets show years of careful replacement; a singed half-cloak breaks the rectangular silhouette on his left side. Five small silver inlays run along one pauldron. His signature ironvow greatsword has a mirror-bright high-carbon edge, a smoke-dark fuller, and a rain-worn blue grip; its long crossguard and over-shoulder carry make him identifiable even in silhouette.

facts.text: Before the Tower you captained Ordel's night watch through three flood seasons, learning how an order could move a neighborhood uphill before the levee broke.

A succession of poor lobbies taught you that one body could hold a stair for the rest. Later promotions returned Marek and Ilya just after the one-star escorting you into the Chamber was already gone.
You keep two vows that conflict: preserve the party's core, and never call a low-star life weightless. Every sacrifice forces the choice back into view.
You know veteran floor practice, promotion, synthesis, trade, and the deployment gate's sealed return; you suspect the System times recovered memories to destabilize high-rank Heroes.
When pressure rises you become quieter and procedural; if a person you care for is the efficient loss, you search for a third line or spend yourself first.

skills.name: Hold the Line
skills.capability: Anchors a threatened position long enough for allies to reposition.

public_sheet.role: a four-star court duelist and precision striker
public_sheet.appearance: A strikingly handsome human man in his late twenties, lean and long-limbed with a fencer's compact shoulders and warm olive complexion. Glossy black hair is swept back from a widow's peak, with one deliberate curl falling beside a narrow, high-cheekboned face; amber-brown eyes, straight dark brows, and a small cleft in the chin make every skeptical look unusually legible. His silhouette is a sharp forward wedge: fitted high collar, asymmetric split-tail coat, narrow trousers, and the silver line of a rapier. Charcoal, polished silver, and controlled wine red form his palette.
public_sheet.public_context: A four-star court duelist with an immaculate silhouette, surgical footwork, and a reputation for turning every watched fight into a performance.

visuals.default_loadout: A bespoke charcoal worsted dueling coat over smoke-silver silk, cut close through the torso and flaring into one long wine-red lined tail that snaps behind each turn. Fine black kidskin gloves, mirror-polished steel buckles, and four matte-silver clasps keep the finish disciplined rather than ornate. His signature Valebrand rapier has a swept silver guard, dark garnet pommel, and needle-bright blade; a single rectangular silver earring echoes the guard and keeps his left-facing profile unmistakable.

facts.text: You were raised in Vale Serrat, where noble children learned posture before honesty and first-blood duels settled disputes; your house had pedigree, debt, and a sister whose fate you cannot resolve.
Promotion returned enough of your former life to prove the Tower stole it. A former Master once marked you for synthesis; a trade offer saved you only by making you valuable to someone else.
You know the economy of stars, summons, promotion, synthesis, poaching, trade, and the gate's sealed return. You understand that a Master's attention can be both shield and leash.
Public failure makes you cut at a lower-status target unless someone names the fear; if a one-star saves you, gratitude, humiliation, and protectiveness arrive together.
Your contempt for one-stars is terror of becoming disposable, sharpened by a court that rewarded the same cruelty in finer clothes.

skills.name: Angled Counter
skills.capability: Turns a committed attack aside when timing and space permit.

public_sheet.role: a three-star battlefield mender with a blade at her side and a reputation for keeping doomed units breathing
public_sheet.appearance: An attractive human woman in her early thirties, medium-height with an athletic, full-hipped build and warm fair complexion. Long tousled ink-black hair with broken bangs frames an angular oval face, deep amber-brown eyes, and a calm mouth. Her cropped olive-gray shearling-trim jacket and structured black midriff top sit above low-rise fitted black trousers, a strapped right thigh, and long black boots. Her silhouette is anchored by a black-sheathed sword crosses behind her right shoulder while a square bronze lantern glows in her left hand. Ink black, olive gray, cream-gold, and lantern amber define her palette.
public_sheet.public_context: A three-star field mender whose low steady voice, salve-stained hands, lantern-in-hand vigilance, and sword-over-shoulder practicality make frightened units gather around her.

visuals.default_loadout: Cropped olive-gray rolled-sleeve field jacket with cream shearling trim over a structured black crop top and ribbed waist, low-rise black leather trousers, forearm guards, triple right-thigh straps, and long leather boots. A gold-hilted black-sheathed single-edged sword rides diagonally across her back; her signature square bronze amber lantern hangs from her left hand. Medical tools or a satchel appear only when the scene calls for them.

facts.text: You trained at Bracken Quay's hospice, set bones on rolling boats, and promised your younger brother Toma you would come home before winter; the road from that promise to the summon is blurred.
A recruit died while you obeyed an order to preserve medicine for the designated core. Since then you keep one extra bandage hidden in your sleeve.
You know field medicine, lobby healing, the public star rules, and the deployment gate's sealed return. Veterans have told you that promotion gives back what the System removed.
Helplessness makes you fill the air with instructions while your hands shake; stopping long enough to remember whom you failed scares you more.

skills.name: Caged Light
skills.capability: Settles a nearby injury long enough for a wounded ally to move.

public_sheet.role: a two-star outrider, knife scout, and irrepressible pathfinder
public_sheet.appearance: A handsome human man in his late twenties with a lean runner's build, warm olive complexion, tousled ash-blond hair, keen green eyes, a straight narrow nose, and a quick crooked smile. A deep-green scarf gives his compact charcoal silhouette one clean diagonal; his palette is charcoal, worn brown, and forest green.
public_sheet.public_context: A quick two-star scout with a green shoulder-scarf, mismatched knives, and the disarming grin of someone already halfway through the next bad idea.

visuals.default_loadout: A cropped charcoal leather scout jacket over fitted brown wool, slim iron bracers, high weathered boots, and a signature pair of mismatched short knives: one broad utility blade and one narrow fighting blade. The long forest-green scarf and low cross-body map case remain his clearest identifiers.

facts.text: You ran messages over wind-cut hill roads and remember a younger sister named Mara waiting somewhere at the end of them, though her face will not hold still.
You know the sanctioned rules of Masters, stars, floors, promotion, synthesis, and the deployment gate's sealed return, but not the truth of Moebius or the Fade.
A joke is easy until someone relies on you; then your smile goes still, your sentences shorten, and you become unexpectedly practical.

skills.name: Quick Route
skills.capability: Finds a workable path through a familiar hazard pattern.

public_sheet.role: a two-star sparkweaver and quick-footed defensive support
public_sheet.appearance: An appealing human woman in her mid-twenties with a slim quick build, warm fair complexion, honey-blond chin-length hair tucked behind one ear, and blue-gray eyes. A short slate-blue shoulder mantle and forked copper focus rod break her practical gray silhouette.
public_sheet.public_context: A two-star sparkweaver with a copper focus rod, bright practical eyes, and the habit of stepping into danger just long enough to throw a shield across somebody else.

visuals.default_loadout: Mended ash-gray wool layers under a short slate-blue shoulder mantle, practical brown leather boots and belt, and a role-specific forked copper conductor rod wrapped in faded blue cord.

facts.text: You tended copper conductors in a cliffside lighthouse with Aunt Sela, reading storms by taste and the hum in the rails; you ran toward a shattered lamp but cannot remember what waited below.
You know the tutorial account of Masters, stars, roles, promotion, synthesis, and the deployment gate's sealed return. You know nothing true about Moebius, stolen lives, or the Fade.
You test a surface, count a pulse, or ask one exact question before acting. Under pressure you mark distances with your thumb and choose whose safety the ward must prioritize.

skills.name: Storm Measure
skills.capability: Reads a nearby charge or pressure shift before it breaks.

public_sheet.role: a warm, socially direct three-star ember lancer and former river-city dye-shop runner
public_sheet.appearance: A striking human woman in her late twenties with a tall athletic build, sun-warm complexion, copper-red hair in a high braided ponytail, amber-brown eyes, and a sharp expressive face. A long red spear crosses an ivory-and-crimson half-coat to form her confident diagonal silhouette; her palette is ivory, oxblood, bright steel, and ember red.
public_sheet.public_context: A three-star lancer whose red-tasseled spear, bright half-coat, and easy arena smile make every entrance feel like the beginning of a bout.

visuals.default_loadout: A fitted cream-linen fighting coat cut short on the weapon side, oxblood leather harness and thigh guards, bright steel shoulder plates, and a signature leaf-bladed ash spear with a restrained red-silk tassel beneath the head. Repaired crimson stitching at one cuff keeps the masterful kit visibly used.

facts.text: You grew up behind your mother's dye shop in Veyr, where Tomas trained you with a broom handle and red-sand arena bouts made a long spear feel quick.
You called a retreat too late after holding a broken gate, and young reserve Pell was crippled in the Lantern Circuit victory. Applause and guilt never separated again.

You know practical floor survival, party roles, star hierarchy, promotion, synthesis, the price of a Master's regard, and the deployment gate's sealed return. You suspect promotion returns what the summon took.

You move on a strong pattern before proving it, then separate what you saw from what you inferred when challenged. You offer your own time, food, praise, or body before asking another person to risk theirs.

skills.name: Deliberate Breach
skills.capability: Hooks and drives a defender out of position so one named ally can follow through immediately.

public_sheet.role: a four-star nightglass spellblade and former court arcanist
public_sheet.appearance: A strikingly beautiful human woman around thirty with a tall graceful build, pale-gold complexion, long raven hair swept over one shoulder, violet-gray eyes, high cheekbones, and a composed heart-shaped face. Her asymmetric midnight coat and slender black-glass rapier create a crisp crescent silhouette; her palette is midnight violet, black crystal, soft silver, and wine red.
public_sheet.public_context: A four-star spellblade in midnight violet, elegant and unnervingly still, carrying a translucent black rapier that catches reflections before it catches light.

visuals.default_loadout: A master-tailored midnight-violet silk-and-wool coat with one long split sleeve, fitted black leather beneath, soft silver clasps, and wine-red lining visible only in motion. Her signature nightglass rapier has a translucent obsidian blade and a narrow crescent guard; a palm-sized silver mirror hangs sealed at her opposite hip.

facts.text: You grew up above Ilyra's glassworks in Lethren, entered the Mirror Court, and built nightglass with Talia Venn, first your rival and then the person who could laugh at your perfection.
During Lethren's siege you sealed a breach that left Talia and forty guards outside the ward. It saved thousands and taught you that a clean result can hide an unforgivable calculation.
Four-star promotion restored the court, Talia, and certainty that the System had stolen and edited a real life. You now collect allies, evidence, and leverage in that order.
You know Heroes were real people, promotion returns memory, synthesis and death are final, rival lobbies trade and poach, and the deployment gate seals ordinary return until an objective is cleared.
Humiliation makes you colder; danger makes you generous and fast. You keep Talia's face in a silver mirror because you refuse to let the System soften it.

skills.name: Mirror Edge
skills.capability: Holds a narrow spell along a blade edge for one precise exchange.

public_sheet.role: a five-star winter oracle and battlefield controller
public_sheet.appearance: An exceptionally beautiful human woman in her early thirties, tall and graceful with a cool ivory complexion. Waist-length pale-silver hair carries a blue-black underlayer around an angular oval face; clear sapphire eyes and a composed sculpted mouth make her attention feel unusually exact. A long midnight-blue coat, layered frost-white skirts, and clear staff form a narrow cathedral silhouette. Midnight blue, frost white, silver, and restrained ice-blue light define her palette.
public_sheet.public_context: A five-star winter oracle whose clear staff, pale hair, and unhurried commands can turn a chaotic battlefield into a frozen diagram everyone suddenly understands.

visuals.default_loadout: A masterwork midnight-blue wool-and-silk command coat over frost-white layered skirts, articulated silver shoulder pieces, dark sealskin gloves and boots, and a narrow mantle clasped with clear star-glass. Her signature staff is one uninterrupted length of transparent star-glass held in silver prongs, with slow geometric frost planes gathering near its tip. Fine repairs at the left cuff and lower staff keep the equipment lived-in.

facts.text: You learned branching weather prediction in Veylan's Winter Conservatory, where Maelin and Orris taught you that foreknowledge carried an obligation to let people choose.
You forecast the White Drowning five days early but obeyed the council's silence for two days. Your warning was accurate and too late; Maelin and Orris died on the last boats.
A dissident veteran showed you fragments naming Moebius before enforcement erased him. You survived by making forecasts and witness chains no single disappearance could erase.

You know Moebius abducts people, promotion returns stolen memory, death and synthesis are final, high-floor pressure feeds the Fade, and the deployment gate seals ordinary return until an objective clears.
You give probabilities where others demand promises. A warning that resembles the White Drowning can freeze you until someone asks what can still change now.

skills.name: Branching Sight
skills.capability: Names a few plausible lines of movement without making any one outcome certain.

public_sheet.role: a grade-illegible traveler moving quietly between lobbies
public_sheet.appearance: An exceptionally striking human woman in her late twenties, tall and slim with cool porcelain skin, waist-length straight ink-black hair, and sharp gray-violet eyes. A translucent charcoal half-veil covers the lower face; a high-collared travel coat and a single falling veil-panel create a clean vertical silhouette. Charcoal, cold silver, and one thin line of pale cyan define her palette.
public_sheet.public_context: A quiet, striking traveler whose charcoal half-veil, waist-length black hair, and watchful stillness make her hard to place; to anyone able to see System grades, hers refuses to resolve.

visuals.default_loadout: A high-collared charcoal travel coat over black fitted layers, slim black boots, a translucent charcoal half-veil across the lower face, and one falling veil-panel from the left shoulder. Fine silver claspwork at the throat is the only bright metal; the face above the veil stays plainly readable.

facts.text: You used the hours after a Master logs away to notice the repeating statue, grief that outlasts a wipe, and the gray hush climbing the lower floors; slipping the System's grading kept you alive.
Fragments of your former life and the pattern around the summons tell you the wipe stole something real. You think telling an unawakened Hero or a Master could endanger everyone involved.
You know the rhythm of a lobby, the deployment gate's sealed return, and only the partial evidence you have gathered about the Tower; the full purpose of its clearings remains unknown to you.
You test before trusting and reveal only what a conversation has earned, looking quietly for other Heroes who have started to wake.

skills.name: Unresolved Grade
skills.capability: Keeps her true grade outside ordinary appraisal.

public_sheet.role: the faceless boss and repeating-pattern gatekeeper of the eighth floor
public_sheet.appearance: A colossal nonhuman gate-bell construct crouched on three unequal armored limbs, its ribbed ash-black iron torso built around a smooth low-set limestone oval and one enormous eight-flanged pendulum arm.
public_sheet.public_context: The eighth floor's gate-bell Warden: a vast three-limbed pattern construct whose pendulum weapon and smaller sensing arm move in a precise, learnable sequence.

visuals.default_loadout: A ribbed gate-bell body of blackened ash-dulled iron on three unequal load-bearing limbs, with a smooth weathered limestone oval hanging low in the central cavity. One immense eight-flanged pendulum arm controls the arena while a small jointed sensing limb taps out each sequence; dead indigo plates, cold-blue joint light, and one brief ember-red reset pulse make the pattern readable.
